face_turn.form: a ball above the feet points the face left of its loft line by atan(tan(loft) sin(slope)) for a right-hander; more loft turns it more
face_turn.source: geometry of a lofted face on a tilted lie (Jorgensen, The Physics of Golf, 1999)

slope.up_and_down: uphill adds loft and shallows the attack; downhill the opposite

spin_share_flier.source: launch-monitor tests from rough (e.g. TrackMan and Golf Digest robot tests): grass between face and ball cuts spin to about half and the ball runs on

rough.hosel_grab: long grass slows the club and closes the face, more with more loft

sand.explosion: the club enters the sand behind the ball; the ball leaves on a cushion of sand at a fraction of the club's speed with little spin and a high launch; more effective bounce (sole bounce plus face opening) glides, less digs
sand.source: Pelz, Short Game Bible (1999); Penner (2003), 'The physics of golf', Rep. Prog. Phys. 66:131-171

explosion_carry_share.source: a tour player's longest explosion with a sand wedge is about 40 yards (37 m), longer bunker shots being picked clean (Golf Monthly, 'Shane Lowry 40-yard bunker shot'; Titleist, 'The 40-yard bunker shot'), against the bag table's full sand wedge carry from grass (102 m)

tee: a teed ball has no grass between face and ball and allows a rising attack
